record.interface_detail: REST API v1 with an apikey; rate limits are per account per minute, shared between key and cookie sessions, and every response carries X-RateLimit-Limit and X-RateLimit-Remaining.
record.tooling: Documented REST API (including /downloads, /torrents, /usenet, /hosts, /user/limits), browser extensions, WebDAV, Discord and Telegram integrations advertised on the home page.
record.chaining: One of only three services here that carries usenet, and the cheapest of them at EUR 4.99 for 30 days; with 80+ hosts plus NZB plus a torrent cloud it can replace two subscriptions, as long as the files stay under 200 GB.

record.price_per_tb_month: EUR 4.99 per 30 days, flat; EUR 32.99 per year (EUR 2.75/month)
record.notes: The annual term at 32.99 EUR is the lowest per-month price of any service - 2.75 EUR - and the reason this record exists separately from the free tier. The first two are documented; the third is documented as unrefundable. The vendor's API endpoint was not located, so the error strings for this service are unverified and the record does not claim any. Free tier is a trial in shape, not in name: 5 links a day with reduced host coverage and no named expiry. The only provider in the set with a documented price rise inside the window: the entry term went from EUR 3.99 to EUR 4.50 between 2023-10-26 and 2024-10-02, +12.8%, and has not moved since. The free tier moved the other way in the same period, from 4 to 5 links a day, so what the free user got improved while what the paid user paid rose. The comparison corpus lists EUR 4.99/30 days; no pricing page was found at /pricing (404), so the price is not repeated as a verified number here. The contradiction is the finding: the product page sells a cloud the FAQ says does not exist. Until a logged-in account shows a file surviving a session, the conservative vendor statement governs. The price is the gap. A third-party review claims USD 4.99 and lists 'Credit card payments, Bitcoin, Hysterium, litecoin' - 'Hysterium' is not a coin, which is a fair measure of that source's care, so nothing from it is carried into this record.

card.summary: Inherits the Deepbrid account tier. The site's own FAQ: 'With the free account you will be able to fetch up to 5 cloud provider links every day.'

record.category: hosted debrid bot (file-host link to download link)

free_tier.stated: Inherits the Deepbrid account tier. The site's own FAQ: 'With the free account you will be able to fetch up to 5 cloud provider links every day.'
free_tier.notes: the bot has no separate allowance; it reads the account behind the API key

per_object_cap.stated: No per-file cap is published for the bot. The paid trial advertises a '200GB Max Download Size', which is a plan ceiling, not a per-object one.
per_object_cap.notes: the 200 GB figure belongs to the 14-day trial listed at EUR 4.50

retention.stated: Nothing is stored: the bot returns a premium URL from Deepbrid's download servers. The life of that URL is not stated on the page read.

egress.terms: No Telegram traffic. 'Generate premium links, manage torrents, check your stats' in a private chat; the bytes come from premium-dl.deepbrid.com.
egress.free_allowance: none: the free allowance is a link count, not bytes

record.interface_detail: A private Telegram chat. Setup is '/setkey <api_key>': 'Store your Deepbrid API key. The bot validates it immediately and deletes your message for security.'
record.tooling: Any Telegram client plus a Deepbrid account API key from the Devices page. Torrents and usenet are accepted as magnets, .torrent and .nzb files dropped in the chat.
record.chaining: Turns a magnet, .nzb or 80+ file-host links into a premium URL without leaving Telegram, so the retrieval path is Deepbrid's servers, not Telegram's; needs a paid plan for volume.

limits.value: 5 cloud-provider links/day on a free account
'200GB Max Download Size' on the paid trial only

record.binding_note: Five links a day is the free wall; a link count is not a byte quota, so the failure mode is 'no more links today', not 'quota exhausted'.

identity_cost.detail: The bot needs a Deepbrid account's API key, so the account must exist first. The signup fields were not read; email is the minimum such an account implies and is not confirmed.

record.reliability_note: Per-hoster daily traffic and link limits apply and the bot can show them but not raise them; an invalid or rotated API key stops the bot with /checkkey.
record.confidence_note: The 5-link free allowance and the API-key mechanism are on the vendor pages read on 2026-10-23. Whether the bot answers a message was not tested (no Telegram account in on 2026-10-23).

evidence.proved: '/setkey <api_key> Store your Deepbrid API key.' and 'Send magnet links, drop .torrent or .nzb files directly in chat' and 'Per-Hoster Limits - View your daily traffic and link limits per hoster in real time'
'With the free account you will be able to fetch up to 5 cloud provider links every day.'
paid tiers: '14 Days Trial EUR 4.50' with '200GB Max Download Size'
the handle resolves to a bot titled 'Deepbrid - Official Telegram Bot' with a Start action

record.price_per_tb_month: not comparable: sold as link counts and plan bandwidth, not bytes
record.notes: Abandon if /setkey disappears or the free link count changes. The bot is a remote control for a debrid account: it adds no Telegram capacity and is not a way to store bytes.

card.summary: Five files a day and a 1.2 GB maximum file size, on free hosts only. The logged-out downloader page shows the panel 'Files per day 0 / 5', 'Filenext Files 0 ...

free_tier.stated: Five files a day and a 1.2 GB maximum file size, on free hosts only. The logged-out downloader page shows the panel 'Files per day 0 / 5', 'Filenext Files 0 / 3' and 'Maximum File Sizes: General 1.2 GB, Filenext 300.0 MB, Emload 300.0 MB'.

per_object_cap.stated: 1.2 GB per file generally; 300 MB on Filenext and Emload

retention.stated: not applicable: no storage is offered on the free account; downloads are proxied to the caller

egress.terms: Five files a day at a 1.2 GB maximum is 6 GB a day, 180 GB a month, if every file lands at the cap. The site also warns that 'some providers have daily limits' even on paid plans.

record.interface_detail: REST API v1 (https://www.deepbrid.com/api/v1) with an apikey, documented publicly, including a /user/limits endpoint.
record.tooling: Documented REST API with per-account rate limits and X-RateLimit headers; browser extensions for Chrome, Firefox, Opera and Edge; a WebDAV path advertised in the integrations strip.
record.chaining: Enough to fetch a handful of small files a day from hosts not subscribed to, and not enough for anything larger than a 1.2 GB file, which rules out most media and any dataset.

record.notes: The numbers are on the vendor's own downloader page and the per-file cap is the one that matters: it is the only service whose free tier refuses a file by size rather than by count. The ladder multiplies 5 x 1.2 x 30 = 180 GB, which stands as a per-session ceiling but is not proven repeatable across two accounts or two addresses. The 1.2 GB cap is the number hit first, and it is 300 MB on two of the listed hosts.
